digest.component_or_area: jira data center adapter transport layer
propositions: The DC transport must be built on pycontribs/jira and confined to an opt-in [jira-datacenter] extra with lazy importing to preserve rebar's zero-dependency contract and raise clear install-naming errors when the extra is missing.

Every TicketTransport method must return raw payload shapes (not jira.Issue objects) that existing mappers consume, with retries only for transient faults (ConnectionError, Timeout, TimeoutError) and never for HTTP errors, following the same 2s/5s backoff as the Cloud transport.

The DC backend must reject non-HTTPS base_url with ConfigError unless allow_insecure=true is explicitly set, verify TLS certificates never disabled (options['verify'] never False), and support ca_bundle for internal CAs — asserted against the actual parameter form the library reads, not vacuous kwarg absence.

Configuration (JIRA_URL, JIRA_PROJECT, JIRA_PAT, ca_bundle, allow_insecure, resolved_statuses) must fail loudly on ConfigError rather than degrade to env-only, and resolved_statuses must configure the absence probe's resolved-status set defaulting to {Resolved, Done, Cancelled}.

The DC backend must self-register into _backend_registry via an import side effect in adapters/__init__.py so select_backend('jira-datacenter') resolves after importing adapters, raising BackendRegistryError (not KeyError) if the import is missing.

All 13 TicketTransport/SupportsLinks/SupportsComments/SupportsAbsenceProbe methods (create_issue, get_issue, update_issue, transition_issue_by_name, add_label, search_issues, set_relationship, get_issuelinks_map, map_remote_links, link_payload_for_relation, add_comment, get_comment_map, probe_remote) must pass live tests against the J5 harness, with transitions verified against server-declared destination status and unknown assignees raising BackendAssigneeNotFoundError on apply while the resolver reports (None, True, False).
